chapter: Wider talk: bands, places and players
title: Tom Brown and the St. Charles Hotel group
summary: He recalls Tom Brown's trombone and his brother's bass playing with Whiteman and Goldkette.

story.theme_name: Trombonists: who they heard, admired and learned from
story.community_name: Talking trombonists: who played the slide and how

blocks.x: Oh, let me see. Did you know Tom Brown in those days?
Tom Brown, he played trombone with, with, uh, with, uh, Johnny Wiggs.

And, uh, um, and Dr. Shushaw and, uh, when we played the St. Charles Hotel there. Yeah. He played good trombone, you know, he played, because he, he first went to New York and, and had musical clowns, see? Mm-hmm. Something like that was his band. I don't know whether he talked, talked to him or not.
Yeah, but not enough, you know, I used to talk to him in his, in the big, you know. Well, he was a brother of Red Brown and played string bass with the Rhythm Kings.
He played wonderful bass. Oh, great.
And later on, he was with Weidman's band, you know. Mm-hmm.
And Goldcat, yeah. Yeah. With Gene Goldcat's band there, too.
He really swung that band. Yeah. When Goldcat would give him a chance, he'd really swung out. Yeah, that's right.
And Vixen always with the band.
